evidenceSources.description: Constructed-state mechanical probes: scoring riders, accelerator sequence, counter predicate matrix
348-game exploratory policy pilot in core-advanced-authority; 16 seed clusters per pairing
Original 216-game pilot run, combined into the 348-game completion set
Static read-only audit of current runtime vs rulebook vs upstream; identifies implementation divergences
Mechanical interaction graph and hypergeometric reachability values (earlier evidence epoch)

evidenceTiers.A: Direct source fact: rulebook, verified engine behavior, constructed-state probe, static audit
evidenceTiers.B: Exploratory or earlier-epoch evidence: policy pilot, historical balance reports
evidenceTiers.C: Inference from mechanics and reachability, not directly tested
evidenceTiers.D: Weak or contradicted evidence; do not rely on alone

statisticalConventions.wilson95: Descriptive marginal intervals, not paired-data inferential intervals
statisticalConventions.pairedBootstrap: Seed-cluster percentile bootstrap95 of mean win-credit (draw=0.5), 10000 resamples
statisticalConventions.signTest: Exact two-sided sign test on positive vs negative seed AB/BA win-credit contrasts
statisticalConventions.holmCorrection: Supplementary Holm-adjusted p-values; no multiplicity correction in original pilot
statisticalConventions.noPooling: Different pairings reuse seeds; games must not be pooled as independent observations
statisticalConventions.noSelfPlayInference: Self-play is not evidence of cross-policy superiority
statisticalConventions.notObservableIsNotZero: Absence of evidence is not evidence of absence

methodology.confidenceConvention: Confidence values are epistemic confidence (0-1), not win probability
methodology.sourceHandling: Read-only treatment of canonical gameplay; SOURCE FACT separated from INFERENCE; policy behavior never treated as optimal play

units.effect: What a card or play does when declared (e.g., Total Clear, Tap, Dig)
units.policy: An implemented heuristic that selects legal actions; not a player and not optimal play
units.sequence: A specific ordered set of declarations within a turn
units.strategicLine: A coherent priority set and sequencing logic
units.archetype: A cluster of lines sharing a primary axis
units.statisticalProfile: The observed behavior and outcome pattern of a policy under pilot conditions

gameModel.deck: 54 cards: 52 standard plus Red Joker and Black Joker
gameModel.swapBar: Two face-down cards plus one face-up card
gameModel.victoryCondition: Secured PR Points >= current Goal at end of player's own completed Full Turn

terminology.QueenGuard: Protects other friendly OTT cards from hostile single-target effects
terminology.BoardLock: Global Black Joker lockdown of non-counter effects, Scuttle, and Trap
terminology.QueensCourt: Exactly two Queens from hand as one multi-card Anchor Play
terminology.Anchor: A card committed to the Enduring Row
terminology.Vulnerable: Aegis-absent and (rules-faithfully) Guard-absent target eligible for Sudden Death

archetypes.name: Score-pressure / race
priorities: Secure high-value points (BJ=11, 10=10, 9=9, 8=8, K=8) as fast as possible
Use tempo only when it materially accelerates victory
archetypes.sequencing: Score on consecutive Mini-Turns; spend 10♥ or 2B+2R only when extra actions convert directly into secured points
archetypes.resourceConversion: cards → PR points; minimal hand preservation
responsePatterns: Counter only what threatens the race (4♠, Board Lock, Sudden Death on key PR)
Ignore disruption that does not reduce secured points below Goal
archetypes.interactionStructure: Forces opponent to answer points rather than build; opponent must spend responses on a clock they did not choose
archetypes.pivotLogic: If opponent holds a reset, shift to preserving a second wave of scoring cards rather than overcommitting to the first wave

archetypes.name: Tempo-compression
priorities: Convert 10♥ (+2 Mini-Turns, cap 3, draw 1) and 2B+2R Ultra (+2 Mini-Turns, draw 2 or rummage 1 Exile) into extra actions and cards
archetypes.sequencing: Accelerator → setup/draw → scoring or disruption within same Full Turn
archetypes.resourceConversion: hand cards + accelerator → action economy → secured points or board control
responsePatterns: Counter the opponent's counter to the accelerator
If accelerator is spent without terminal conversion, the line fails
archetypes.interactionStructure: Compresses multiple turns of value into one Full Turn; strong when opponent cannot answer acceleration or when extra actions convert directly into secured points
failureConditions: Opponent answers the key scoring play the acceleration was building toward
archetypes.pivotLogic: If accelerator is countered or fizzled, fall back to value/conversion line rather than forcing a second accelerator

archetypes.name: Control / suppression
archetypes.sequencing: Disrupt opponent's key plays; lock the board; win the long game on accumulated advantage
archetypes.resourceConversion: cards → denied opponent value → eventual scoring advantage
responsePatterns: Hold counters for highest-value opponent plays
Use structural resets at peak opponent commitment
archetypes.interactionStructure: Suppresses opponent's plan rather than executing its own; strong when opponent cannot simply score through disruption
failureConditions: Control player falls behind in PR and cannot recover
Control cards spent without reducing opponent secured points
archetypes.pivotLogic: If behind in PR, abandon control and race; if opponent's hand is empty, shift to hand-attack or direct scoring
archetypes.pilotCaveat: Implemented control policy underperformed heavily in the pilot; this is policy-behavior evidence, not strategic-line weakness evidence

archetypes.name: Value / conversion
priorities: Use Dig/Recycle/Deep Draw (5, 6, 6♠, ⭐6) to find higher-value conversions
archetypes.sequencing: Draw/filter → accumulate flexible resources → convert at peak value
archetypes.resourceConversion: low-value cards → draw/filter → high-value cards → secured points or board control
responsePatterns: Respond only when opponent threatens a terminal play
archetypes.interactionStructure: Trades early tempo for late-game card quality and flexibility
failureConditions: Immediate score pressure kills before saved resources convert
Window closes before value line can deploy
archetypes.pivotLogic: If under lethal pressure, convert saved resources into immediate scoring or a structural reset rather than continuing to filter

archetypes.name: Fortress / anchor
archetypes.sequencing: Establish Queen protection → anchor key cards → accumulate protected ER → win on durability
archetypes.resourceConversion: Queens + Aegis sources → protected board state → long-term scoring advantage
archetypes.interactionStructure: Makes board expensive to attack; opponent must find K♠, 4♠, ⭐4, or ⭐2 to breach
archetypes.pivotLogic: If opponent holds K♠ or 4♠, do not overcommit to Queen's Court; shift to scoring or tempo

archetypes.name: Reset / structural
archetypes.sequencing: Wait for peak opponent commitment → reset → rebuild
archetypes.resourceConversion: single high-value card → full board state change
responsePatterns: None directly; structural effects are not counterable by ordinary Ace/King authority
archetypes.interactionStructure: Erases opponent's board investment; particularly valuable against high-PR boards, Aegis-heavy states, and Queen fortresses
failureConditions: Reset spent at low opponent commitment
archetypes.pivotLogic: If reset would erase more of user's board than opponent's, hold it; if behind, use it to equalize rather than to gain advantage

archetypes.name: Late-resource / Exhausted
archetypes.sequencing: Track DP depth → preserve anchor/point capacity → convert non-DP resources as DP empties
archetypes.resourceConversion: GY/Exile cards → playable cards when DP is empty
responsePatterns: Anchor lines remain live when Draw is constrained
Recycle and Exile recovery bypass DP
archetypes.interactionStructure: Gains value as DP approaches empty; can turn resource deficit into a race around Exhausted tiebreaks
failureConditions: Anchor/point capacity insufficient to close the game
archetypes.pivotLogic: If opponent is racing and DP is not yet empty, do not wait for Exhausted; score or disrupt now

archetypes.name: Niche hand/board attack
archetypes.sequencing: Identify opponent's key component → attack it → exploit the gap
archetypes.resourceConversion: attack cards → denied opponent components → exploitable window
responsePatterns: None directly; opponent's answer is to play the component before it is discarded
archetypes.interactionStructure: Denies exact components, not generic value; strategic job is to prevent a specific play
failureConditions: Attack fails to prevent a meaningful conversion
Attack card worth more than denied component
archetypes.pivotLogic: If opponent's hand is empty or attack misses key component, do not repeat; shift to scoring or structural play

interaction_graph.diagnosis: Intrilex exhibits a conditional counter-web with local cycles and soft hierarchies, not a clean rock-paper-scissors or four-way cycle
structuralReasons: Counter relationships are typed by declaration class, not by generic card strength
Many effects transform into other lines (K♠ Wild, 10♦ copy, 7/⭐7 nested plays, 2B+2R conversion)
Structural effects bypass ordinary protection (4♠ bypasses Guard, Aegis, Q♠, ordinary immunity)
Protection is conditional (Aegis blocks many effects but not 4♠; Guard blocks single-target but not row-wide; Queen's Court answered only by K♠)
Line value changes with game state (PR total, opponent score, response class, DP depth, GY/Exile density, Queen fortress state, Board Lock status, Exhausted state, hand size, Mini-Turn spent)

axes.description: Score-pressure forces opponent to answer points; control answers plays but does not score
Tempo-compression spends cards for extra actions; value/conversion preserves cards for higher-value later plays
Fortress makes board expensive to attack; reset erases the board
Spending an accelerator reduces hand; holding a counter preserves hand
Hand attack denies specific components; value is denial of exact card, not generic control
As DP empties, anchor lines and GY/Exile access become more valuable

localCycles.conditions: Score-pressure beats control only if it scores through disruption; control beats fortress only if it lands disruption before stabilization; fortress beats score-pressure only if it locks the board
Tempo beats control if acceleration converts to points; value beats tempo if tempo strands its hand; tempo beats score-pressure if acceleration outpaces the race

counterMatrix.note: Predicate matrix from current runtime. Declaration-time gate for super-ace and ultra-three-red is missing (see implementation divergences), so in practice these can target any stack item in the current engine.

reachability.note: Hypergeometric reachability values, not win probabilities

alternativeClassificationsConsidered.name: rock_paper_scissors
alternativeClassificationsConsidered.reason: No stable three-way cycle; counter relationships are typed by declaration class and conditional on game state

alternativeClassificationsConsidered.name: four_way_cycle
alternativeClassificationsConsidered.reason: No stable four-way cycle; more than four functional lines exist and their interactions are typed and conditional

alternativeClassificationsConsidered.name: hierarchy_with_soft_counters
alternativeClassificationsConsidered.reason: Local soft hierarchies exist in specific game states (e.g., fortress with two untapped Queens is locally dominant against ordinary effects), but no universal dominance order exists

alternativeClassificationsConsidered.name: no_stable_cyclical_structure
alternativeClassificationsConsidered.reason: No stable global cycle, but local conditional cycles exist; 'no stable structure' overstates the absence of local structure

metagame_model.justification: The interaction graph is typed (by declaration class), conditional (by game state), and asymmetric (by reachability). Local cycles exist but are conditional on timing and reachability. A soft hierarchy exists in specific local states, but no line is globally dominant. The structure is best described as a conditional counter-web with local cycles and soft hierarchies.
metagame_model.humanMetaNote: No human play data exists. The pilot is policy-conditioned and exploratory. No metagame claim is justified without human validation.

globallyStrong.note: Pilot suggests score-rush and hybrix-rusher-hard are candidates, but evidence is exploratory and policy-conditioned. Mechanically, score-pressure is globally strong because it forces the opponent to answer a clock, but it is not universally dominant.

broadlyReliable.note: Value was close to even against score-rush, hybrix-rusher-hard, and tempo in the pilot. Mechanically, value/conversion is reliable because it preserves flexibility, but it can lose to immediate pressure.

matchupDominant.note: Tempo dominated control (87.5%, Holm p=0.00439) but lost to value (40.6%) and hybrix-rusher-hard (34.4%). Mechanically, tempo-compression is matchup-dominant when opponent cannot answer acceleration.

niche.note: Niche lines have specific jobs under specific conditions; they are not weak, they are conditional.

pareto_frontier.note: No line is high on all six dimensions. Reset and late-resource are on the frontier for specific axes but are dominated in some dimensions by fortress or control. Line choice is a bet on which dimensions will matter in the current game state.

niche_lines.name: Hand raid (3, ⭐3 Super Raid, 9 Anchor discard, RJ opponent attack)
niche_lines.purpose: Deny opponent's exact component (Ace, K♠, Queen pair, Ultra ingredient)
niche_lines.target: Large or overcommitted opponent hand holding a specific card
conditions: Attack card worth less than denied play
niche_lines.cost: A card and a Mini-Turn that do not directly score
niche_lines.failureSignal: Opponent hand already small, or attack misses key component
niche_lines.pivot: If attack misses, do not repeat; shift to scoring or structural play

niche_lines.name: BoardLock (BJ Quick)
niche_lines.purpose: Suppress non-counter effects, Scuttle, and Trap for one Full Turn
niche_lines.target: Opponent who depends on effects/Scuttle/Trap to answer the board
conditions: Opponent plan relies on effects rather than scoring
BJ not needed for 11-point scoring value
Opponent lacks ⭐A or 3-Red to answer Board Lock
niche_lines.cost: BJ (11 points) spent on disruption rather than scoring
niche_lines.failureSignal: Opponent scores through the lock, or holds ⭐A/3-Red
niche_lines.pivot: If opponent scores through, abandon Board Lock and race; if opponent holds ⭐A, do not commit BJ to Board Lock

niche_lines.name: Sudden Death (RJ+BJ or four-of-a-kind, Unrestricted only)
niche_lines.purpose: Scrap a Vulnerable enemy OTT card and start a 2-turn countdown to GY
niche_lines.target: High-value enemy PR or ER card that is not Aegis-protected (and rules-faithfully not Guard-protected)
conditions: Countdown will complete before opponent can recover
niche_lines.cost: RJ+BJ or four cards of a rank — substantial resource investment
niche_lines.failureSignal: Target has Aegis, opponent holds ⭐A, countdown will not complete before opponent wins
niche_lines.pivot: If target is Aegis-protected, do not commit; if opponent holds ⭐A, hold Sudden Death for a window after ⭐A is spent
niche_lines.implementationDivergence: Engine target check is Aegis-only; rulebook Vulnerable should also respect Guard and rank/state immunity

niche_lines.name: ⭐4 Row Exchange
niche_lines.purpose: Swap rows with opponent, taking their PR/ER and giving them yours, plus Aegis on non-Nines
niche_lines.target: Opponent with a superior board (high PR, strong ER, Queen fortress)
niche_lines.cost: Two 4s and the user's current board
niche_lines.failureSignal: Opponent board not better than user's, or opponent can immediately reset or score back
niche_lines.pivot: If exchange does not clearly improve position, hold the 4s for Total Clear or ordinary Row Clear instead

niche_lines.name: 10♠ Stack Theft
niche_lines.purpose: Steal the top of the opponent's stack mid-resolution
niche_lines.target: High-value opponent effect or scoring play on the stack
conditions: Opponent has committed a valuable card to the stack
niche_lines.cost: 10♠ (10 points if scored) spent on theft rather than scoring
niche_lines.failureSignal: Stack empty or low-value, or opponent can counter the theft
niche_lines.pivot: If stack is low-value, score the 10♠ instead

robustFindings: Implemented control policy underperformed heavily against score-rush, tempo, value, and hybrix-rusher-hard
Only Holm-adjusted comparisons surviving multiplicity: score-rush vs control (p=0.00439) and control vs hybrix-rusher-hard (p=0.00122)
Tempo performed well against control but poorly against value and hybrix-rusher-hard
Score-rush was close to even against tempo, value, and hybrix-rusher-hard
No broad stable three-way cycle was established
notSupported: Control as a strategic line is weak — this is policy weakness, not line weakness
Scoring always beats control in human play — no human data exists
A global ranking of strategic lines — sample size and policy set are insufficient

implementation_divergences.description: super-ace and ultra-three-red declarations do not call targetAcceptsCounter at declaration time; can target any stack item including point plays and draws
implementation_divergences.rulebookSays: ⭐A and 3-Red have specific target-class restrictions; point plays, draws, swaps, and passes are not counterable by these authorities
implementation_divergences.engineDoes: Allows ⭐A and 3-Red to target any top stack item
implementation_divergences.source: Static audit of core-authority.js declaration paths

implementation_divergences.description: No royalShieldProtected flag is set in Core; Base/Anchor Aces can counter Royal Shield-protected ordinary effects as if unprotected
implementation_divergences.rulebookSays: When declarer controls more untapped Queens OTT than opponent, Base/Anchor Ace counters are blocked on protected plays
implementation_divergences.engineDoes: Does not implement the pre-declaration Queen-count comparison
implementation_divergences.source: Static audit of core-response.js and core-authority.js

implementation_divergences.description: Voltage 4 requires exact rank+suit match and publishes the guess in the public event
implementation_divergences.rulebookSays: Rank-only match → score/effect; suit-only match → draw; both → rank branch; else return to top; guess is private
implementation_divergences.engineDoes: Succeeds only if both rank and suit match; serializes guessRank/guessSuit in public event

implementation_divergences.description: Generated Seven / Topdeck Casting supports only one generated effect card, no hand components, no Super/Combo, no physical-Seven recursion; ⭐7 scraps chosen effect cards
implementation_divergences.rulebookSays: Revealed generated card may be played for effect, scored, or used in Super/Combo; may combine with hand cards; physical Seven may recurse
implementation_divergences.engineDoes: Truncated to one generated effect; ⭐7 scraps effect cards instead of resolving them
implementation_divergences.source: Static audit of core-private-choice.js:465-571 and core-advanced.js:292-321

implementation_divergences.description: Scoring BJ gives 11 points with no Exile Recycle follow-up
implementation_divergences.rulebookSays: Scoring BJ triggers Exile Recycle (move up to 2 Exile cards to top/bottom of DP)
implementation_divergences.engineDoes: core-score moves BJ to PR with no recycle trigger

implementation_divergences.description: Scoring a Seven gives 7 points with no reveal-top-2-take-one trigger
implementation_divergences.rulebookSays: Scoring a Seven triggers reveal top 2, take one to hand
implementation_divergences.engineDoes: core-score moves Seven to PR with no trigger

implementation_divergences.description: Only 10♣ Foundation effect grants Aegis, not the 10♣ point play
implementation_divergences.rulebookSays: 10♣ scored for points enters PR with Aegis until next Start
implementation_divergences.engineDoes: core-score does not grant Aegis; only Foundation does

implementation_divergences.description: Goal 9 is not available in current Core path
implementation_divergences.rulebookSays: Ordinary +3 or +5 opponent goal shift; 9♠ also reduces own goal by 2
implementation_divergences.engineDoes: ranks.js still resolves goal-shift-nine but core-effects.js does not enumerate it and core-autonomy.js does not list it
implementation_divergences.source: Static audit of core-effects.js and core-autonomy.js

implementation_divergences.description: Natural 4 is not implemented in current unrestricted runtime
implementation_divergences.engineDoes: Listed in ranks.js modes and profile exclusions but no resolver or autonomy candidate exists
implementation_divergences.source: Static audit of ranks.js and core-response.js

implementation_divergences.description: Sudden Death target check is Aegis-only; does not check Guard or rank/state immunity
implementation_divergences.rulebookSays: Target must be Vulnerable (Aegis-absent and Guard-absent and not rank/state-immune)

unresolved_questions.question: No human play data exists; pilot results may not reflect human strategic value
Pilot studied core-advanced-authority only; Sudden Death, ⭐3/⭐5/⭐6/⭐7, and other Unrestricted-only tools were not tested in paired play
HYBRIX adapter calls choose only, not notifyOutcome/recordEnemyAction; opponent-learning is not validated
16 seed clusters per pairing is exploratory; 32 or 64 seeds would narrow bootstrap intervals
How often does a player who holds the right counter class actually use it before it is discarded or stolen?
State-injection experiments placing a Queen fortress against various breach tools would measure breach probability and cost
Inject Board Lock and 4♠ into controlled states and measure their effect on opponent conversion rates
When is spending 10♥ on tempo worse than scoring it for 10 points?
When is holding 2B+2R for a later turn better than firing it immediately?
Inject Exhausted states and measure the value of anchor lines, GY/Exile access, and non-DP resources

claim_ledger.claim: Intrilex is a conditional counter-web, not RPS or a four-way cycle
Counter relationships are typed by declaration class
K♠ is the only standard direct counter to Queen's Court and Royal Marriage
4♠ Total Clear bypasses Guard, Aegis, Q♠, and ordinary immunity
Score-pressure forces the opponent to answer a clock
Implemented control policy underperformed in the pilot
Control as a strategic line is weak
Tempo-compression is matchup-dominant against slow control
No human metagame is established
⭐A/3-Red declaration-time gate is missing in current engine
Royal Shield is not enforced in Core
claim_ledger.source: static audit of core-response.js and core-authority.js

claim_ledger.claim: BJ scores 11 points with no Exile Recycle in current engine
Probe confirmed ordinary scoring of 7♣, 10♣, and BJ reaches PR correctly
Probe confirmed two-accelerator sequence used four declarations with no fizzle
Pilot produced 348/348 canonical terminations with zero errors
Pilot mirrors were incomplete (5-6 games per policy, not planned 16)
No unrestricted-profile pilot was completed
Reachability values are hypergeometric, not win probabilities
Specific singleton in opening 5-card hand is ~9.3%
Total Clear access (one of 4♠/2♠/K♠) in opening 5 is ~25.7%
2B+2R Ultra in opening 5 is ~60.1%
Product version is 1.0.0, engine 4.2.6, rules 4.3.1
Default profile is core-advanced-authority, ranked is core-unrestricted-authority
